assets.title: Ящики и короба
assets.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Primary request: Transfer the EXACT hand-painted fantasy game-prop visual style of the supplied images to a transparent reference sheet of merchandise for filling the merchant stall.
Input roles: Image 1, the original crate, and Image 2, the original bucket, are the primary STYLE anchors. Image 3, our corrected merchant stall, specifies continuity of palette, faceted merchandise shapes and simplified planar cloth. Images 4 (anvil) and 5 (weapon rack) are supporting STYLE references for chunky proportion, bold bevels, broadly painted timber and plain metal only. Do NOT reproduce the whole stall, the anvil, the weapons or any furniture. Preserve the supplied painted rendering language while replacing the subject with the four merchandise units listed below.
STYLE IS CRITICAL: chunky BEVELED and deliberately carved geometry, broad polygonal corner facets, warm honey/ochre-brown timber with a few large visible painted strokes per board, strong coherent colour planes, plain dark grey iron and oversized round rivets. Rounded shapes are faceted into a manageable number of broad hand-painted planes. Cloth and sacks have just 2 to 5 large angular folded colour planes, like the parcels and rolls in Image 3. Clean volumetric form and readable silhouette at the high gameplay camera. This is DRAWN stylized 3D game concept art, not a realistic product render. NO photorealism, NO PBR-looking materials, NO photographic wood grain, NO pores, NO realistic textile weave, NO microtexture, NO fine noisy scratches, NO realistic cloth simulation. No thick black comic outlines. Match the crisp chunky painterly treatment of the actual references.
Palette: warm rich honey-brown and ochre wood; plain desaturated dark iron; faded olive and warm cream/oatmeal fabric; muted earthy brown leather; subdued orange terracotta and charcoal pottery. A few clear large colour masses, no decorative painted patterns.
Composition: exactly FOUR distinct merchandise units in a spacious 2-by-2 layout. Each quadrant contains ONE independent prop or ONE compact physically coherent group. Do not show the same object from multiple views. Units have broad transparent gaps and never overlap or touch between quadrants. Every complete silhouette and base must fit comfortably within its quadrant; ample margins at all image edges. No panels, dividing lines, frames, captions, labels, numerals or text. Each unit fills much of its quadrant so it can be cropped independently for Tripo. High-resolution square sheet.
Camera: all four units shown in the same orthographic-like elevated front three-quarter view, approximately 45 to 48 degrees above horizontal, similar to Image 3 and the gameplay camera. Show the top, side faces and full base of every unit. Keep believable relative size within the set, and use only minimal perspective.
Construction: large clear seams and joints, thick rims and handles, broad durable straps and twine with no dangling filaments. Closed and open volumes must make physical sense. Every unit stands or lies stably on its own flat base, ready to sit on a counter or shelf. No attached shelf, plinth, ground, rug or support platform.
Presentation: neutral, even albedo-like colour visibility with simplified PAINTED form shading. Broad painted bevel colour accents as in the references, not realistic directional highlights. No directional sunlight, sunset cast, dramatic contrast, lighting sources, glow, hard cast shadows or shadow beneath any prop.
Background: genuine fully transparent alpha including every gap, handle opening, and space between units. No black, white or coloured opaque backdrop, no checkerboard, gradient, scene, floor, environment or horizon.
Hard exclusions: text, symbols, runes, logos, labels, emblems, flags, banners, heraldry, crests, shields, weapons, characters, animals, vegetation, lamps, lanterns, candles, torches, fire, smoke, sparks, glowing liquids, coins or tiny loose clutter. Merchandise only, not any part of the merchant stall itself.

FOUR UNITS FOR THIS SHEET: upper left, one chunky closed square wooden packing crate with an X-shaped timber brace, broad honey-coloured planks, heavily bevelled corner posts and plain dark iron corner bands, visually matching the original crate style; upper right, one low wide rectangular closed wooden supply box, broad plank lid and exactly two plain iron bands, with a clean horizontal silhouette; lower left, one compact stack of TWO closed crates of different sizes, small crate resting fully on the larger crate, a stable single prop group with clearly distinguishable edges; lower right, one shallow open wooden goods box holding exactly THREE large cream and olive wrapped rectangular cloth parcels, with thick box walls and clearly readable tied packages above the rim. Very few strong painted wood-grain strokes. No ornamented treasure chest.
